Kevin — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so we have alignment going into the technical follow-up:

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary concern: predictable latency for patient-facing inference (95th pct SLO target: 200ms) during peak windows (07:00–20:00 ET).
- Regulatory: logs/audit trail must be retained for 12 months, and keys must be customer-controlled for Protected Health Information.
- Team preference: start with Hosted API for speed, but open to Dedicated or Private if isolation/certification gaps are blocking.

Open technical questions for Medicorp:
1) Typical concurrency and token distribution for patient workflows (we asked for a sample 24-hour token histogram).
2) Tolerance for occasional tail latency spikes vs. hard SLOs (is a 1-hour window of degraded latency acceptable if compensated by retries/backoff?).
3) Any procurement or network constraints for a Private VPC deployment (e.g., allowed VPN setups, IP allow lists, SOC 2 evidence needed).

Proposed next steps:
- We’ll share a short SLO matrix that maps deployment modes to expected tail behaviors and mitigation pathways (attached: slo_matrix.pdf).
- Technical deep-dive with Marissa (serving runtime lead) to validate KV-cache sizing and prefix-caching strategy — propose Tue 2027-03-23 at 11:00 AM ET.
- Medicorp to send the 24-hour token/concurrency sample and any vendor whitelist rules.

Attachments: medicorp_scoping.xlsx (POC data points template), slo_matrix.pdf (redwood SLO tradeoffs by deployment mode).

Thanks — if the meeting time works I’ll send a calendar invite.

Kevin / Anika — quick technical notes ahead of today’s deep dive: feel free to forward to your infra lead.

1) Hybrid: Hosted + Customer Keying — we can support customer-managed keys for encryption-at-rest via KMS integration on Hosted, but network isolation (VPC peering / VPN) requires Dedicated or Private. For PHI boundary guarantees we typically recommend Dedicated or Private when keys + network isolation are both mandatory.

2) Isolation model tradeoffs (short):
- Hosted: fastest onboarding, shared hosts with soft isolation (prefix / KV caching per customer). We offer priority routing and per-customer capacity shaping but cannot promise noise-free hardware.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools for your account; strong throughput predictability and reduced noisy-neighbor jitter. Still multi-tenant at hypervisor level unless you take Private on-prem.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full network isolation, customer-managed control plane, required for strict regulatory/risk profiles.

3) SLO behaviors and mitigations:
- For the 95th/99th percentile targets: Dedicated reduces variance by eliminating cross-customer scheduling contention; we also provide automatic spike buffering and hot-path caching for short bursts.
- In Hosted, we use smart fallback routing to compatible model variants when capacity is constrained — this reduces p99 outage risk but can change latency/cost.

4) VPN & IP allowlist: we can support an always-on IPSec tunnel for Private/Dedicated setups; Hosted generally requires static egress IP ranges (we can provide them) for allowlist configuration.

I’ve attached the SLO matrix and a small POC scoping template (medicorp_scoping.xlsx) — filled the sections we discussed.

Agenda for today’s call (technical deep-dive):
- Medicorp token histogram review (you)
- Sizing: KV cache & batch window tradeoffs (me)
- Routing & fallback policy options (Ben)
- Next: propose POC plan and timeline

See you on the call.
